name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q01 - Identification of brown alga from morphology

questiontext.text: Identify the marine brown alga shown in the given diagram, which possesses a holdfast, midrib, frond, and air bladders, and exhibits a diplontic life cycle.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Diagram Interpretation and Given Features
The given diagram illustrates a branched, thalloid marine alga attached to the substratum by a holdfast. Its leaf-like photosynthetic organ (frond) has a prominent central midrib and distinct air bladders.

Step 2: Conceptual Principle
Members of Phaeophyceae (brown algae) typically have a plant body differentiated into a holdfast, stipe, and frond. Among the common brown algae, Fucus is characterised by dichotomously branched fronds bearing a midrib and air bladders for buoyancy. Furthermore, while most algae are haplontic and some brown algae like Ectocarpus and kelps are haplo-diplontic, Fucus is a notable exception that exhibits a diplontic life cycle.

Step 3: Evaluation of Other Genera
Laminaria has a simple, unbranched blade-like frond on a distinct stipe without air bladders along a midrib. Dictyota has a ribbon-like dichotomously branched thallus lacking air bladders and a midrib. Ectocarpus is a simple, branched filamentous brown alga.

Step 4: Final Answer
The marine brown alga shown in the diagram is Fucus.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q02 - Ploidy and nutrition in moss phases

questiontext.text: The given diagram shows a moss (Funaria) with two distinct parts labeled as Gametophyte and Sporophyte. Which of the following statements accurately describes the ploidy and relationship between these two phases?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Diagram Interpretation
The diagram shows the leafy gametophyte of Funaria anchored by multicellular, branched rhizoids along a main axis bearing spirally arranged leaves, with the sporophyte (composed of foot, seta, and capsule) attached at the apex of the gametophyte.

Step 2: Conceptual Principle
In all bryophytes, including mosses, the main, dominant, independent, and photosynthetic plant body is the haploid (n) gametophyte, which produces gametes. After fertilisation, the diploid (2n) zygote develops into a multicellular diploid sporophyte.

Step 3: Evaluation of Relationship
The sporophyte in bryophytes is not free-living; it remains attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it. Meiosis occurs in the capsule of the sporophyte to produce haploid spores, which germinate to form the protonema stage of the gametophyte.

Step 4: Final Answer
The gametophyte is haploid and photosynthetic, whereas the sporophyte is diploid and attached to the gametophyte, deriving nourishment from it.

answer.text: The gametophyte is haploid and photosynthetic, whereas the sporophyte is diploid and derives nourishment from the gametophyte.
The gametophyte is diploid and non-photosynthetic, whereas the sporophyte is haploid and independent.
Both the gametophyte and the sporophyte are haploid and independently photosynthetic.
The sporophyte is diploid and free-living, whereas the gametophyte is reduced and dependent on the sporophyte.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q03 - Identification and classification of horsetail pteridophyte

questiontext.text: Examine the given diagram of a pteridophyte showing a terminal strobilus, distinct nodes and internodes, whorled branches, and an underground rhizome. Identify this plant and the class of Pteridophyta to which it belongs.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Diagram Interpretation
The diagram depicts a vascular plant (pteridophyte) with an underground rhizome bearing roots, an erect stem clearly differentiated into nodes and internodes, whorls of branches arising at the nodes, and a compact terminal cone-like structure called a strobilus.

Step 2: Conceptual Principle
Pteridophytes are classified into four classes: Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida, and Pteropsida. Horsetails belong to the genus Equisetum, which is characterised by jointed stems with distinct nodes and internodes, whorled branches, and sporophylls forming compact strobili (cones).

Step 3: Taxonomic Classification
Equisetum is placed in the class Sphenopsida. In contrast, Selaginella belongs to Lycopsida, Psilotum belongs to Psilopsida, and ferns such as Dryopteris belong to Pteropsida.

Step 4: Final Answer
The pteridophyte shown in the diagram is Equisetum, and it belongs to the class Sphenopsida.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q04 - Haplo-diplontic life cycle phases and examples

questiontext.text: The given diagram represents a haplo-diplontic life cycle pattern with two multicellular phases marked A and B. Which of the following correctly identifies A and B along with the plant/algal groups that exhibit this pattern?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Diagram Interpretation
In the given haplo-diplontic life cycle diagram, region A includes syngamy, the diploid zygote (2n), the multicellular sporophyte, and meiosis leading to haploid spores (n). Region B includes the haploid spores (n), the multicellular gametophyte (n), and gametogenesis leading back to syngamy.

Step 2: Identification of Phases A and B
Therefore, A represents the diploid (2n) sporophytic phase and B represents the haploid (n) gametophytic phase. Both phases are multicellular in a haplo-diplontic life cycle.

Step 3: Evaluation of Plant and Algal Groups
All bryophytes and all pteridophytes exhibit the haplo-diplontic life cycle pattern (with bryophytes having a dominant gametophyte and pteridophytes having a dominant sporophyte). While most algae are haplontic (e.g., Volvox, Spirogyra), some algal genera such as Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, and kelps also exhibit a haplo-diplontic life cycle. Seed-bearing plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) and the alga Fucus follow a diplontic life cycle.

Step 4: Final Answer
A represents the diploid (2n) sporophytic phase and B represents the haploid (n) gametophytic phase, and this pattern is exhibited by all bryophytes, all pteridophytes, and algae such as Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, and kelps.

answer.text: A is the haploid (n) gametophytic phase and B is the diploid (2n) sporophytic phase; exhibited by all gymnosperms and angiosperms.
A is the diploid (2n) sporophytic phase and B is the haploid (n) gametophytic phase; exhibited by all bryophytes, all pteridophytes, and algae such as Ectocarpus and Polysiphonia.
A is the diploid (2n) sporophytic phase and B is the haploid (n) gametophytic phase; exhibited by Fucus, Volvox, and Spirogyra.
A is the diploid (2n) sporophytic phase where meiosis occurs in the zygote, and B is the haploid (n) gametophytic phase; exhibited exclusively by bryophytes.
